predicate over a finite separable L/kappa(t); and `isOpen_chartLocus` is dat-b row B-4's

1	# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)
2	
3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
5	workspace.
6	
7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
8	
9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
13	
14	```bash
15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
24	
25	Archon-Commit: agent
26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
29	```
30	
31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
34	
35	### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed
36	
37	Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
38	was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
39	`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).
40	
41	The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
42	publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
43	The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
44	describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
45	including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
46	the shared index drifts behind.
47	
48	Consequences, all three binding:
49	
50	1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
51	   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
52	2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
53	   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
54	   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
55	   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
56	3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
57	   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
58	   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).
59	
60	Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
61	the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.
62	
63	## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there
64	
65	`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
66	directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
67	that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
68	path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
69	15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:
70	
71	```bash
72	LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
73	while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
74	  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
75	  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
76	  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
77	  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
78	    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
79	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
80	      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
81	    fi
82	    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
83	    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
84	       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
85	      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
86	    fi
87	  fi
88	  sleep 10
89	done
90	echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
91	# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
92	```
93	
94	Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
95	- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
96	- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
97	  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
98	  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
99	  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
100	  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.
101	
102	## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes
103	
104	uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
105	(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
106	build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
107	retry-looping.
108	
109	## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)
110	
111	`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
112	sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
113	in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
114	YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
115	`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
116	other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
117	HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
118	only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
119	root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.
120	
121	### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)
122	
123	The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
124	2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
125	worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
126	sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
127	The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
128	i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.
129	
130	So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:
131	
132	> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
133	> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
134	> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
135	> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
136	> usually accompanies it.
137	
138	This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
139	still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
140	warning.
141	
142	**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
143	other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
144	exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
145	their work and turns one incident into two.
146	
147	## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only
148	
149	No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
150	`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
151	workspaces must use their own lock paths.
152	
153	### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)
154	
155	The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
156	projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
157	over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building
158	`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the sibling project. Same failure as the
159	OpenGA incident, not covered by the rule as written.
160	
161	The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
162	`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
163	(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
164	at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.
165	
166	### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan
167	
168	§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
169	`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
170	not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
171	also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
172	provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.
173	
174	Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:
175	
176	* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
177	  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
178	* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
179	  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
180	  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
181	  check you substituted.

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)

*2026-07-19, Fable design lane (`AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-b`, worksheet-first).  BINDING
parents: `informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §2.3 (V-rel-B), §4 DAT-B row, §5 risk 7 (the

## §0 Verdicts up front

### §0.1 The deliverable is frozen by landed code — DAT-B is ONE instance plus its feed

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161-169`) already consumes
exactly what Stage C needs:

```
noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy (Over.mk (…))
```

`f`/`hf` are DAT-C's (w4-datc §3.2–§3.3, frozen).  **DAT-B = the
`Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective` instance** (mathlib
`CategoryTheory/Sites/LocallySurjective.lean:94`: `imageSieve_mem` — every section of
`pic0SigmaSheaf` is Zariski-locally in the image of the chart family), plus the
injectivity bookkeeping of §2 (which turns out to be LANDED, §0.4) and the qc/effectivity
export for DAT-J (§3.3).  Elementwise (`imageSieve`, `LocallySurjective.lean:38-52`):
for every scheme `T`, structure `a : T ⟶ Spec k`, and `λ ∈ pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`
(`Picard/Pic0Functor.lean:107`, membership `Iff.rfl` `:121`), the opens on which
`(a, λ)` restricts to a chart value must cover `T`.  With DAT-C's CHART-U(a)/(c)
(w4-datc §3.3) this reduces to the **pointwise coverage theorem** (§1.2): the chart
loci `{chartLocus c λ}_{c}` cover `T`.

### §0.2 The main structural finding: coverage proper is FIELD-LEVEL; RE-5/engine enter only through the shared openness brick

The parent §2.3 chain (extraction → RE-5 → engine → transport) is where the roadmap
title's "RE-5 descent + engine" live — but in the landed architecture that chain is
the mechanism of **CHART-U(b)** (openness of the chart locus, co-owned with DAT-C,
§1.6), NOT of the coverage theorem itself.  Membership of a point `t` in a chart locus
is a statement about the FIBRE class at `κ(t)` alone (CHART-U(a) is a field-point
predicate), so the coverage theorem is a per-fibre field-level argument:
degree bookkeeping (landed, §1.3) + the h⁰-drop normalization (B-1, §1.4) + the
separable-point density transfer (B-2, §1.5).  Consequences, each a route-around
recorded so no prover rebuilds retired machinery:

1. **The RE-5 (1d-ii) seam is NOT on DAT-B's path.**  `DatumDescent.lean:38-49` records
   "threading the kernel onto `H⁰(D.sheaf)` on the nose is the remaining (1d-ii)
   clause … the one open SEAM".  DAT-B never threads `H⁰` across `B₀ → B`: the
   openness brick consumes the engine over the stage (`descentRigidEngine`,
   `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547`) and transports only OPENS (preimage) and
   CLASSES (`descent_cechPicClass`, `:525`), never section modules.  The seam stays
   with the DAT-1 lane; nothing here gates on it.
2. **The m-strata do NOT collapse** (correcting a tempting simplification): DAT-0a's
   uniform bound `b` (`RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean:71`) is a bound *per field*
   `b = b(Y_K, π_K)`, and per I-0204/I-0234 ledger constants never transport across
   `k → κ(t)`.  So the twist exponent `m` in the chart index must range: at a fibre
   `L` the coverage argument picks `m_t` with `m_t·d₁ ≥ b_L + …` against the fibre's
   OWN DAT-0a instance (§1.4 step 3).  Statements quantify `∃ c = (m, Σ)`; no uniform
   `m₀` exists.  (Per-chart membership stays a single collapsed condition — parent §5.5
   discipline unaffected.)
3. **DAT-B needs NO relative high-twist certificate.**  w4-datc §3.4 expects DAT-B to
   need CERT-Σ "at high twist" (the parent §2.2.3a projective-generator argument).  In
   the design below the high-twist divisor presentation is needed only at FIELD fibres
   (the DAT-J effectivity export, §3.3), where the FIELD dictionary suffices — the
   `hsurj` completion (B-3, §1.7), not relative CERT-Σ.  The only relative certificate
   DAT-B consumes is DAT-C's own CERT-Σ at degree `g`, through CHART-U(c), untouched.

### §0.3 The staging DECISION (parent §5.7 residue): sep-closed assembly level; finite-level extraction is post-glue and owned by DAT-glue/DAT-G

**Decided:** the coverage theorem (hence the 01JJ assembly) is stated at a
**separably closed instantiation** `K_s` of the standing pack (a separable closure of
`k`; every Stage-B statement is generic in its base field, so this is an
instantiation, not new machinery).  The chart index is the full DAT-C index
`c = (m, Σ)` with `Σ` an effective `CurveDivisor` on the `K_s`-curve — an INFINITE
`Type u` index, which mathlib's 01JJ accepts as-is (`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/
Representability.lean:56-58` takes any `ι : Type u`).  Coverage at a FIXED finite
separable level is **neither claimed nor needed**: the per-fibre drop argument
requires rational points adapted to the fibre (the parent §2.5(d) genus-2/ℚ
obstruction is exactly this), and no proof at finite level is known to this design.

**The finite-level extraction is post-glue**: once `J_{K_s}` exists, its chart images
are OPEN (each chart is an open subfunctor of the now-represented functor), they cover
`J_{K_s}` (coverage), and `J_{K_s}` is quasi-compact by the DAT-J image argument
(`|J| =` the image of the qc `DivScheme` under the Abel morphism — `compactSpace_divScheme`
`Picard/DivSchemeQProj.lean:194` + the §3.3 effectivity export).  A finite chart
subfamily follows topologically; its finitely many `Σ_i` (finitely many `K_s`-points
of a finite-type scheme) are defined over one finite separable `k'/k`, which is how
`k'` is CHOSEN.  Descending the representing property from `K_s` to `k'` (so that
DAT-G's finite-Galois Speiser machinery applies from `k'` down to `k`) is a genuine
brick **nobody's scoreboard carries** (the w4-ddr9 §0.2 pattern): named here
**DAT-G0 — finite-level transfer of the representing datum** (spreading out the
finite chart/gluing data + the fpqc-locality of "yoneda(J) ⟶ pic0-sheaf is an iso").
It belongs to the DAT-glue/DAT-G boundary, NOT to DAT-B; this worksheet's obligation
is to have FLAGGED it (orchestrator echo, end note).  Nothing in §1–§2 depends on how
DAT-G0 is discharged.

### §0.4 Injectivity is LANDED — the second half of the node title is bookkeeping

Every injectivity/separation input the 01JJ engine needs is in the tree (§2): the
big-site sheaf certificate `pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:90`
region, bundled `:147`), the arbitrary-test separation and S-lemma
(`pic0Subgroup_ext_of_le_cover` `Picard/Pic0ZariskiSheaf.lean:263`,
`mem_pic0Subgroup_of_cover` `:277`), the affine basic-open half
(`PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq`, `Picard/PicEtAffZariskiSep.lean:137`), (C1) étale unit
injectivity (`PicEtAff.unit_injective` `Picard/EtaleSeparatedness.lean:16`,
closed via `unit_injective_of_ker` `Picard/EtaleSeparatednessClose.lean:193`), and the
classify-uniqueness (`IsDivRepClassify` + `divClassifyZar` ∃!-form,
`Picard/DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90/:206`).  The chart-functor mono is DAT-C's §3.2.
**DAT-B builds no injectivity file**; §2 records the consumption map so no lane
re-proves any of it.

### §0.5 Launchability summary (details §4)

* Launchable NOW, field-level, no gates: **B-1** (drop normalization), **B-2**
  (separable-point density), **B-3** (field-dictionary `hsurj` completion — F4
  `divRepClassifyZar` is landed, I-0243, so the DivScheme-point corollary closes too).
* Launchable after a one-note co-sign with the DAT-C lane: **B-4** (CHART-U(a)
  arbitrary-plus-class spelling + CHART-U(b) openness — every chain input landed:
  extraction `Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`, RE-5
  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:514`, engine open `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean:221`).
* Gated on DAT-C names only (their C5, launchable now on their plan): **B-5** (the
  pointwise coverage theorem).
* Gated on divRep(F7)+CERT-Σ through DAT-C's C9: **B-6** (the `IsLocallySurjective`

### §0.6 Standing context

The w4-datc §0.5 pack verbatim (= the `DivRepClassifyZar.lean:56-81` context), at the

105	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
106	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
107	
108	noncomputable section
109	
110	/-! ## The split witness predicate at a class over a field -/
111	
112	variable (C) in
113	/-- **The split witness predicate** (CHART-U(a) in the `w4-datb` §1.6 (a-amendment)
114	spelling), at a plus class `μ` over a field `K`.
115	
116	A plus class over a field need not be an honest Čech class — it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for
117	an étale cover `E` of `K`.  The amendment's "for some finite separable `L/κ(t)` splitting
118	the collapsed plus class" is this: there is a finite separable extension `L/K` over which
119	`μ` becomes `relPicMk` of an honest Čech class `M` on `C_L`, and `M` admits an effective
120	witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
121	
122	Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
123	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
124	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
125	
126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
127	
128	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
129	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
130	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
131	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
132	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
133	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
134	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
135	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
136	with it the openness route.
137	
138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
139	
140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
141	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
142	  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
144	  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
145	  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
147	  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
148	  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
149	  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
150	  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
151	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
152	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
153	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
154	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
155	      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
156	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
157	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
158	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
159	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
160	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
161	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
162	
163	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
164	
165	variable (C) in
166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
168	
169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
182	
183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.
192	
193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
198	GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be
200	injective.  At `−g` the same anchor gives `h⁰ = 1 − 2g`, negative for `g ≥ 1` — the contradiction
201	that made the locus empty. -/
202	theorem degAt_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
203	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T)
204	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
205	    degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) t
206	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
207	  rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
208	    degAt_sigmaFamily, (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hlam) K t]
209	  ring
210	
211	/-- **`chartTwist` inverts `chartValue`'s twist** — the sign check, as a theorem rather than a
212	docstring claim.
213	
214	Applying `chartTwist` to a chart value returns the Abel class it came from.  This is the
215	statement that was FALSE of the earlier definition (which returned
216	`abelDiv · Σ² · (θᵐ)⁻²`), and it is why the direction is now pinned by the kernel: any future
217	edit to `chartTwist` that breaks the inversion breaks this lemma.
218	
219	Recorded per issue I-0514.  A degree ledger alone does not catch a sign error — the wrong-signed
220	ledger was internally consistent — but an inversion law does. -/
221	theorem chartTwist_chartValue {n : ℕ} (m : ℕ)
222	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
223	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
224	    chartTwist C m Z T (chartValue C π n m Z T s) = abelDiv C π n T s := by
225	  rw [chartTwist, chartValue]
226	  group
227	
228	/-! ## CHART-U(a): the locus -/
229	
230	variable (C) in
231	/-- **CHART-U(a), `chartLocus`** (`w4-datc` §3.3, co-signed `w4-datb` §1.6): the set of
232	points of a general test `T` at which the twisted fibre class `λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)` has, after
233	some finite separable splitting of the collapsed plus class at `κ(t)`, an effective witness
234	divisor with vanishing `H¹`.
235	
236	The three layers, each supplied by a named brick:
237	* the *point-to-field-point* passage is `Over.testPoint` (input 0 of this brick — the one
238	  nothing in the tree had);
239	* the *twist* is `chartTwist`, the class-side avatar of `chartValue`;
240	* the *split witness reading over a field* is `IsSplitWitness`.
241	
242	This is the RESERVED name of `Pic0ChartLocusClass.lean`'s header, now defined.  Note it is
243	strictly stronger than `cechWitnessLocus`: general test, twisted class, split predicate. -/
244	def chartLocus (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
245	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) : Set T.left :=
246	  {t : T.left | IsSplitWitness C
247	    (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))}
248	
249	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
250	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left) :
251	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam ↔ IsSplitWitness C
252	      (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)) :=
253	  Iff.rfl
254	
255	/-! ## The datum-layer reading
256	
257	The witness clause of `IsSplitWitness` is stated on a presenting Čech class over `C_L`.
258	The tree's *engine-facing* predicate is stated on a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum`
259	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`), and
260	the two are joined by `exists_cechPicClass_eq` (every class is presented) plus
261	class-intrinsicity.  This is the seam CHART-U(b) crosses to reach
262	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, so it is recorded here as a lemma of the definition
263	rather than left implicit in the openness proof. -/
264	
265	/-- **The witness clause at a splitting field, in datum form**: for a Čech class `M` over
266	`C_L`, admitting an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` is exactly
267	`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` of any datum presenting `M` — as a class over the base `L` itself,
268	where `relCurveMap C L L` is the identity comparison.
269	
270	Note the datum lives over the *field* `L` as base ring, which is the affine base the
271	engine's `PrimeSpectrum L` has a unique point of; that is why the fibre reading and the
272	base reading coincide here. -/
273	theorem exists_witness_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_of_datum
274	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
275	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C L π) {M : (relCurve C L).CechPic}
276	    (hD : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass
277	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M) :
278	    (∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
279	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) M
280	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
281	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1))
282	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := by
283	  rw [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing, hD]
284	
285	/-- **Upward closure of the witness clause along a separable extension of the splitting
286	field** — the substantive half of the (a-amendment)'s "some (equivalently every)".
287	
288	If a Čech class `M` over `C_L` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`, then
289	so does its base change to any finite separable `L'/L`.  This is what makes two splittings
290	of the same plus class comparable: pass to a common separable extension and compare there,
291	rather than comparing the two splittings directly.
292	
293	Proof: present `M` by a datum `D` over `L` (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`); the witness clause at
294	`L` is `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L`, which transfers to `L'` by the co-owned separable
295	invariance `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`
296	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:157` — itself resting only on faithful flatness of a field
297	extension, so separability is packaging, not content). -/
298	theorem exists_witness_of_separable_extension (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
299	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
300	    {L' : Type u} [Field L'] [Algebra k L'] [Algebra L L'] [IsScalarTower k L L']
301	    [Algebra.IsSeparable L L'] (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
302	    (h : ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
303	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
304	          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
305	              ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
306	    ∃ W' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left).CurveDivisor,
307	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L' W' = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L') M
308	        ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
309	            ((C ⊗ overSpec k L').left.divisorSheaf L' W') 1) := by
310	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (C := C) (B := L) (π := π) M
311	  obtain ⟨W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
312	  -- the witness clause at `L` is the datum predicate at `L`: `relCurveMap C L L` acts as
313	  -- the identity comparison on classes, since it is `Spec` of the identity algebra map.
314	  have hid : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C L L) D.cechPicClass = D.cechPicClass := by
315	    have : relCurveMap C L L = 𝟙 (relCurve C L) := by
316	      rw [relCurveMap]
317	      have hom : overSpecMap (k := k) L L = 𝟙 (overSpec k L) :=
318	        Over.OverMorphism.ext (by simp)
319	      rw [hom, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id]
320	      rfl
321	    rw [this, Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
322	    rfl
323	  have hL : D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing L := ⟨W, by rw [hid, hD, hW], hW1⟩
324	  -- transfer along the separable extension, then read it back as a witness clause
325	  obtain ⟨W', hW', hW1'⟩ :=
326	    (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable L L').mp hL
327	  exact ⟨W', by rw [hW', hD], hW1'⟩
328	
329	/-! ## Naturality — the half CHART-U(b) transport (i) consumes -/
330	
331	/-- **`chartLocus` is compatible with restriction of the class**: the twist commutes with
332	`picEtMap`, so restricting `λ` along a morphism of tests restricts the twisted family too.
333	
334	This is `sigmaFamily_natural` + `thetaFamily_natural` and nothing else; it is stated
335	separately because transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6 (the descent-preimage step) is exactly
336	this identity read at the field point of a point over the source. -/
337	theorem picEtMap_chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
338	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) :
339	    picEtMap C f (chartTwist C m Z T lam)
340	      = chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam) := by
341	  rw [chartTwist, chartTwist, map_mul, map_inv, map_mul, map_pow,
342	    sigmaFamily_natural, thetaFamily_natural]
343	
344	/-- **`chartLocus` pulls back into `chartLocus`** — transport (i) of `w4-datb` §1.6, in the
345	form the assembly consumes.
346	
347	For `f : T' ⟶ T` and `t : T'.left`, membership of `t` in the pulled-back locus and of `f t`
348	in the original are the *same* condition on the *same* twisted class, read at two fields:
349	`κ(t)` and `κ(f t)`, with `κ(f t) → κ(t)` the induced extension (`testPointFieldMap`).  So
350	the transport is exactly the invariance of `IsSplitWitness` under that extension.
351	
352	**This lemma proves nothing on its own — it is an interface, and its proof is `hinv`.**  Said
353	plainly so that no lane cites it as if transport (i) were discharged.  What it *does* is fix
354	the exact shape of the obligation and put the burden where it belongs: on the morphism `f`,
355	via the field extension `κ(f t) → κ(t)` it induces, rather than hidden inside the locus.  The
356	tree's landed invariance (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_separable`) discharges `hinv` when
357	that extension is separable — which is the étale-carrier case the (b-amendment) needs, and is
358	*not* automatic for an arbitrary morphism of tests.  The residue between the two is why
359	`hinv` is a hypothesis and not a `rw`. -/
360	theorem mem_chartLocus_of_mem_chartLocus_comp (m : ℕ)
361	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
362	    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (lam : picEt C T) (t : T'.left)
363	    (hinv : IsSplitWitness C
364	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint (T := T) (f.left.base t)) (chartTwist C m Z T lam))
365	      → IsSplitWitness C
366	        (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T' (picEtMap C f lam)))) :
367	    f.left.base t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam
368	      → t ∈ chartLocus C m Z (picEtMap C f lam) :=
369	  hinv
370	
371	end
372	
373	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-! ## The keystone: the greedy drop to `h⁰ = 1` -/

/-- **COV-2, the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop** (★ B-1 keystone, worksheet §1.4):
on the curve bundle `Y` over the field `K` with `χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`, let `P` be an
admissible point oracle — closed points, `K`-rational (`residueDeg = 1`), dense (meeting
every nonempty open).  Then every divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`
admits an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with

  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`.

Induction on `e`: at each step the rank anchor gives `h⁰ = e' + 1 ≥ 1`, the oracle
supplies a rational non-base point (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`), and the exact
drop (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`) preserves the invariant `h¹ = 0` while
lowering the degree budget by one.  The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5) instantiates
`P` with the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points of B-2. -/
theorem exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (g : ℕ)
    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    (P : Set Y)
    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)

section Density

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]

/-- **COV-3, density of base-changed rational points** (★ B-2 keystone, worksheet

nonempty open `W` of the relative curve `C_L = relCurve C L`, some `k`-rational point

`C_L` is affine with sections `Γ(U) ⊗_k L` (`Over.sectionsBaseChange`); a basic open

(`exists_algHom_tensorPointEval_ne_zero`); `D(a)` is nonempty in the reduced curve, and

change evaluates `f` to a nonzero element of `L`
(`gammaSpecIso_appLE_sectionsBaseChange`), hence lies in `D(f) ⊆ W`. -/
theorem Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints [IsSepClosed k]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsIntegral C.left]
    (W : (relCurve C L).Opens) (hW : (W : Set (relCurve C L)).Nonempty) :
    ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left) (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) ∈ W := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨z, hzW⟩ := hW
  -- an affine chart of `C.left` under `z`, and its affine preimage chart of `C_L`
  obtain ⟨U, hU, hxU, -⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset
    (X := C.left) (U := ⊤) (x := (fst C (overSpec k L)).left.base z) trivial
  haveI : IsAffineHom (fst C (overSpec k L)).left :=
    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsAffineHom)
      (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k L)).flip
      (isAffineHom_of_isAffine (overSpec k L).hom)
  have hV : IsAffineOpen ((fst C (overSpec k L)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U) :=
    hU.preimage (fst C (overSpec k L)).left
  have hzV : z ∈ (fst C (overSpec k L)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U := hxU
  -- a basic open of the chart inside `W` around `z`
  obtain ⟨f, hfW, hzf⟩ := hV.exists_basicOpen_le
    (V := W ⊓ ((fst C (overSpec k L)).left ⁻¹ᵁ U)) ⟨z, ⟨hzW, hzV⟩⟩ hzV

    refine Set.mem_of_eq_of_mem hbase ?_

        IsLocalRing.closedPoint k := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    rw [hy]
    exact (C.left.basicOpen_le a) hpmem

section Sigma

variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

variable (C) in
/-- **The Σ-family** (worksheet §3.2): the DAT-5 base-class pullback mechanism reused
at the class `𝒪(Z)` of a Weil divisor `Z` on the base-changed curve `C_k`. -/
def sigmaFamily (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    picEt C T :=
  thetaFamily C (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass k Z) T

variable (C) in
/-- Naturality of the Σ-family: it pulls back to itself under every test map. -/
theorem sigmaFamily_natural (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
    picEtMap C f (sigmaFamily C Z T) = sigmaFamily C Z T' :=
  thetaFamily_natural C _ f

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree of the Σ-family at every field point is `deg k Z`** (E-iv-alg under
the DAT-5 degree law + E-i). -/
theorem degAt_sigmaFamily (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (sigmaFamily C Z T) t = Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
  change degAt (thetaFamily C (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass k Z) T) t = _
  rw [degAt_thetaFamily, classDeg_picClass]

variable (C π n) in
/-- **The chart value** (worksheet §3.2): the Abel value shifted by the Σ-family and
`m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family,
`abelDiv s · sigmaFamily Z · (θ_T^m)⁻¹`. -/
def chartValue (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (s : divFamZar C π n T) : picEt C T :=
  abelDiv C π n T s * sigmaFamily C Z T
    * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m)⁻¹

variable (C π n) in
/-- Naturality of the chart value in the test object. -/
theorem picEtMap_chartValue (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
    picEtMap C f (chartValue C π n m Z T s)
      = chartValue C π n m Z T' (divFamZar.map C π n f s) := by
  rw [chartValue, chartValue, map_mul, map_mul, map_inv, map_pow, picEtMap_abelDiv,
    sigmaFamily_natural, thetaFamily_natural]

theorem degAt_chartValue (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (s : divFamZar C π n T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :

Look for names like pullback, comap, map, baseChange on CurveDivisor; also look at how `Scheme.CurveDivisor` is defined (grep `structure CurveDivisor` / `def CurveDivisor`), what its data is (coefficient function at non-generic points?), and whether there is a degree-compatibility (`deg` of the base-changed divisor) and a picClass-compatibility (`CurveDivisor.picClass` commuting with `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap ...)`). Check files under AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/ named like DegreeBaseFieldInvariance, DivisorBaseChange, ClassCohomology, FLVClass, and anything with BaseChange in the name.

(2) SINGLE-POINT divisors and base change of a k-RATIONAL point. `CurveDivisor.single` exists (used in RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean). Is there a lemma computing the base change / pullback of `single x 1` for a point x whose residue field is the base field (residueDeg = 1)? Look at AlgebraicJacobian/Curve/SepPointsDense.lean and SepPointsDenseKit.lean for `Over.rationalPointBaseChange` and any statement about the image point / fibre being a single point, and any statement relating a rational point of C.left to a point of `relCurve C L`.

(3) THE FIBRE OF thetaFamily/sigmaFamily AS AN HONEST CECH CLASS over a field L. `thetaFamily C c T : picEt C T` for a base class `c : (relCurve C k).CechPic` (check the actual argument type; grep `def thetaFamily`). I need: a lemma that says the fibre of `thetaFamily C c` at a field point `overSpec k L ⟶ T`, read through `picEtAffineEquiv`/`PicEtAff.map`/`PicEtAff.unit`, is `relPicMk` of the base-changed class `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c` — i.e. that theta/sigma families are HONEST (not just plus) classes at every field point, with a computable Čech representative. Grep in Picard/ThetaShift.lean, Picard/ThetaChartClassNaturality.lean, Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean, Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean, Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean. Report the exact spellings available.

(4) THE FIBRE-FIELD UNIFORM VANISHING BOUND. `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` in RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean (check line ~71): give its exact signature and the instance/hypothesis pack it needs (what must hold of the field L and the curve over L). Also report `Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg`, `Sheaf.h0`, `divisorSheaf`, `moduleKSheaf` spellings as used there, and whether there is a landed statement that `Sheaf.chi (moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - g` for the base-changed curve over a field extension L of k (i.e. the χ-invariance under base field extension) — grep for `chi_moduleKSheaf`, `chi` + `baseChange`, `genus`, in RiemannRoch/.

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocus
7	
8	/-!
9	# The unconditional splitting of a plus class over a field (CHART-U(a), input 1)
10	
11	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.2 step 1 and `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 both
12	open with the same move, and both treat it as a step of a longer argument:
13	
14	> restrict along `t`; a plus class over `κ(t)` is `PicEtAff.mk E x`; étale field-cofinality
15	> produces a finite separable `L/κ(t)` over which the class is an honest Čech class.
16	
17	This file makes that move a **named, unconditional theorem** rather than a step, because it
18	is consumed at three separate places (the split predicate `IsSplitWitness`, the coverage
19	theorem COV-1, and the degree seam) and because its statement is exactly the *witness-free*
20	half of `IsSplitWitness`: every plus class over a field becomes an honest Čech class over
21	some finite separable extension.  Nothing here mentions a witness divisor, `H¹`, `θ`, `Σ`,
22	`divRep` or a certificate.
23	
24	## Why this is worth isolating
25	
26	`IsSplitWitness C μ` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean:148`) is an existential over a *tuple*: the
27	extension `L`, its four instances, the presenting Čech class `M`, and then the witness
28	divisor.  Read naively, a consumer proving membership of `chartLocus` has to produce all of
29	them at once, and a consumer *using* membership has to destructure all of them.  But the
30	first six components exist for **every** class, with no hypothesis at all — that is
31	`exists_splitting_of_picEt` below.  So the honest content of `IsSplitWitness` is only the
32	witness clause *at* a splitting, and the two readings are related by
33	`isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness`.
34	
35	That matters for the lane order: COV-1 (dat-b §1.2) can produce its splitting *before* it
36	knows anything about `h⁰`/`h¹`, choose `m` at that field (§1.2 step 3, where the uniform
37	bound genuinely does not exist), and only then run the drop.  Without this separation the
38	`m`-choice and the splitting choice are entangled inside one `∃`.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` — **every plus class over a field is an
43	  honest Čech class over some finite separable extension.**  Unconditional; no witness.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEt` — the same in the `picEt` spelling, which is
45	  the one `IsSplitWitness` is stated against.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness` — the two readings agree:
47	  `IsSplitWitness` is exactly "some splitting carries a witness".  Its `.mpr` is also the
48	  introduction rule; see the closing note for why no positional constructor lemma exists.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
53	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
54	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
55	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
56	
57	universe u
58	
59	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
60	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
61	
62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
63	
64	open AlgebraicJacobian
65	
66	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
67	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
71	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
72	
73	noncomputable section
74	
75	/-! ## The splitting itself -/
76	
77	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
78	-- The presentation lives over the base-changed étale carrier, and closing the existential
79	-- unifies its `Algebra k L` (the derived composite) against the goal's through that carrier
80	-- — the same heavy defeq `PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean` budgets 800000 for.
81	/-- **Every plus class over a field is an honest Čech class over some finite separable
82	extension** (`w4-datb` §1.2 step 1, `w4-datc` §3.3 — the first move of both, here
83	unconditional and witness-free).
84	
85	Given `μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)`, there is a finite separable `L/K` and a Čech Picard
86	class `M` on `C_L` with `μ|_L = relPicMk M` as plus classes.
87	
88	The three steps, each a landed brick:
89	
90	1. `picEtAffineEquiv` (`Picard/PicEt.lean:235`) reads `μ` in `PicEtAff C K`, where by
91	   `PicEtAff.ind` it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for a presented étale cover `E` of `K` and a
92	   descent class `x`;
93	2. étale field-cofinality — `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`
94	   (`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:287`) — refines `E` by a finite separable field `L/K`,
95	   i.e. supplies `ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L`.  This is the step that uses that `K` is a
96	   *field*: over a general base an étale cover has no such refinement;
97	3. `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:101`)
98	   converts the refinement into the presentation.
99	
100	The `k`-algebra structure on `L` and the tower `k → K → L` are *derived*, not chosen: they
101	are the composite `algebraMap K L ∘ algebraMap k K`, exactly as `degAffFieldAlgebraBase`
102	(`Picard/DegreeZero.lean:229`) does it.  Constructing them here rather than demanding them
103	of the caller is the whole ergonomic point — a caller who has only `K` cannot produce them,
104	since `L` does not exist until step 2. -/
105	theorem exists_splitting_of_picEtAff (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
106	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
107	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
108	    (a : PicEtAff C K) :
109	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
110	        (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
111	        (M : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CechPic),
112	      PicEtAff.map C L a = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) := by
113	  -- (1) read `a` as a plus class on a presented cover
114	  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
115	  | mk E x =>
116	    -- (2) refine the cover by a finite separable field
117	    obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hLalg, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨ℓ⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
118	    letI := hLfield
119	    letI := hLalg
120	    letI := hLfin
121	    letI := hLsep
122	    -- the `k`-structure and the tower are the composite, not a choice
123	    letI hkL : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
124	    haveI htow : IsScalarTower k K L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
125	    -- FORGET the composite's VALUE before going further (I-0161-adjacent hazard, measured
126	    -- this session).  Keeping it transparent makes the final `exact` substitute a composite
127	    -- algebra term for the existential's variable, and every `overSpec k L` /
128	    -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left` in the goal is then rechecked against a differently-spelled
129	    -- instance — that defeq does not terminate inside 1600000 heartbeats.  `htow` is a
130	    -- `have`, so it has already forgotten the value it was proved from; nothing downstream
131	    -- needs it.
132	    clear_value hkL
133	    -- (3) the refinement is the presentation
134	    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom C x ℓ
135	    exact ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hLalg, htow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM⟩
136	
137	variable (C) in
138	/-- **The splitting theorem in the `picEt` spelling** — the form every consumer of
139	`IsSplitWitness` meets, since the split predicate is stated on
140	`PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)`.  Immediate from
141	`exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` at `a := picEtAffineEquiv C K μ`; kept separate so that the
142	heavy elaboration of the previous theorem is not re-run through the affine comparison. -/
143	theorem exists_splitting_of_picEt {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
144	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
145	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
146	        (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
147	        (M : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CechPic),
148	      PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
149	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) :=
150	  exists_splitting_of_picEtAff C (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
151	
152	/-! ## The two readings of `IsSplitWitness` -/
153	
154	variable (C) in
155	/-- **`IsSplitWitness` is exactly "some splitting carries a witness"** — the two readings of
156	the (a-amendment) agree.
157	
158	The forward direction is destructuring.  The reverse is `isSplitWitness_of_splitting`.  The
159	point of stating it as an `iff` is that the *left* side is the definition consumers meet and
160	the *right* side separates the two independent choices (which extension; which witness),
161	which is what makes the COV-1 lane order of `w4-datb` §1.2 legal: the splitting is fixed at
162	step 1, the witness only at step 5. -/
163	theorem isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
164	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
165	    IsSplitWitness C μ
166	      ↔ ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
167	          (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
168	          (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
169	        (PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
170	            = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M))
171	          ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
172	              Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
173	                ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
174	                    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) :=
175	  Iff.rfl
176	
177	/-! ## A note on the intro rule that is deliberately ABSENT
178	
179	An `isSplitWitness_of_splitting` taking the twelve components as separate arguments was
180	written and then **removed**, because it cannot be elaborated at acceptable cost and the
181	`iff` above already serves as it: `(isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness C μ).mpr`
182	takes exactly the bundled tuple.
183	
184	The measurement, recorded so nobody re-attempts it: `IsSplitWitness` mixes the two spellings
185	of the base-changed curve — `(relCurve C L).CechPic` for the presenting class and
186	`((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor` for the witness divisor.  Handing the tuple to one
187	anonymous constructor makes Lean unify the seven instance slots while `L` is still a
188	metavariable, re-checking those carriers on each attempted assignment.  Every variant tried
189	(`refine` instead of `exact`; bundling the witness clause as a single `have`; normalising
190	either spelling; routing through the `iff`) still timed out at 1000000 heartbeats.  Going
191	through `.mpr` at a call site where `L` is already fixed costs nothing, because there is then
192	no metavariable to unify around.
193	
194	The general shape of the hazard: a definition that spells one object two ways is cheap to
195	*use* and expensive to *introduce* positionally.  Prefer `Iff.rfl` plus `.mpr` to a bespoke
196	constructor lemma. -/
197	
198	end
199	
200	end AlgebraicGeometry
201

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Over.sectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]

/-- The **relative curve** `C ⊗ Spec R` over the affine test ring `R`: the underlying
scheme of the cartesian-monoidal product of `C` and `overSpec k R` in `Over (Spec k)`. -/
noncomputable def relCurve : Scheme.{u} := (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left

lemma relCurve_def : relCurve C R = (C ⊗ overSpec k R).left := rfl

/-- The relative curve is a scheme over `Spec R` via the second projection. -/
noncomputable instance relCurve.instOver : (relCurve C R).Over (Spec (.of R)) :=
  .ofHom (snd C (overSpec k R)).left

variable (D : C.left.AffineTwoCover)

/-- The **base-changed affine two-cover** of the relative curve: the preimages of the
charts of `D` under the first projection `relCurve C R ⟶ C.left`
(`Scheme.AffineTwoCover.pullbackProd`), an affine two-chart cover of `relCurve C R`. -/
noncomputable def relCover : (relCurve C R).AffineTwoCover := D.pullbackProd R

/-- The first base-changed chart is affine (`G-CBC-1`). -/
theorem relCover_isAffineOpen₀ : IsAffineOpen (relCover C R D).V₀ :=
  (relCover C R D).isAffineOpen₀

/-- The second base-changed chart is affine (`G-CBC-1`). -/

/-! ## The comparison morphism between relative curves over `R → R'` -/

section CurveMap

variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']

/-- `Spec` of the algebra map `R → R'`, as a morphism `overSpec k R' ⟶ overSpec k R`
in `Over (Spec k)`. -/
noncomputable def overSpecMap : overSpec k R' ⟶ overSpec k R :=
  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R R'))) (by
    simp only [overSpec_left, Over.mk_hom, ← Spec.map_comp,
      ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq])

@[simp]
lemma overSpecMap_left :
    (overSpecMap (k := k) R R').left = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R R')) :=
  rfl

/-- **The comparison morphism between relative curves** over the test-ring change
`R → R'`: the underlying scheme morphism of the whiskering `C ◁ overSpecMap R R'`,
`relCurve C R' ⟶ relCurve C R`. -/
noncomputable def relCurveMap : relCurve C R' ⟶ relCurve C R :=
  (C ◁ overSpecMap (k := k) R R').left

/-- The comparison morphism commutes with the first projections. -/
lemma relCurveMap_fst :
    relCurveMap C R R' ≫ (fst C (overSpec k R)).left = (fst C (overSpec k R')).left :=
  congrArg (fun φ : C ⊗ overSpec k R' ⟶ C ↦ φ.left)
    (whiskerLeft_fst C (overSpecMap (k := k) R R'))

/-- The comparison morphism intertwines the second projections through `Spec` of the
algebra map. -/
lemma relCurveMap_snd :
    relCurveMap C R R' ≫ (snd C (overSpec k R)).left =
      (snd C (overSpec k R')).left ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R R')) :=
  congrArg (fun φ : C ⊗ overSpec k R' ⟶ overSpec k R ↦ φ.left)
    (whiskerLeft_snd C (overSpecMap (k := k) R R'))

/-- The comparison morphism pulls the base-changed opens of `C_R` back to the
base-changed opens of `C_{R'}`. -/
lemma relCurveMap_preimage (V : C.left.Opens) :
    relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) =
      (fst C (overSpec k R')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V := by
  rw [← Scheme.Hom.comp_preimage, relCurveMap_fst]

/-- `appLE` is invariant under an equality of morphisms (the inclusion witness is
proof-irrelevant). -/
private lemma appLE_congr_hom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f g : X ⟶ Y} (h : f = g) {U : Y.Opens}
    {W : X.Opens} (e : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ U) :
    f.appLE U W e = g.appLE U W (h ▸ e) := by
  subst h; rfl

/-- **The relative sections comparison map** over the test-ring change `R → R'`: the
ring homomorphism `Γ(C_R, V_R) →+* Γ(C_{R'}, V_{R'})` induced by `relCurveMap`. -/
noncomputable def relSectionsMap (V : C.left.Opens) :
    Γ(relCurve C R, (fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) →+*
      Γ(relCurve C R', (fst C (overSpec k R')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
  ((relCurveMap C R R').appLE ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    ((fst C (overSpec k R')).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (le_of_eq (relCurveMap_preimage C R R' V).symm)).hom

/-- The sections comparison map commutes with the curve pullbacks: pulled-back sections
of the curve compare to pulled-back sections. -/
lemma relSectionsMap_pullback (V : C.left.Opens) (s : Γ(C.left, V)) :
    relSectionsMap C R R' V (relPullbackSection C R V s) =
      relPullbackSection C R' V s := by
  have h : (fst C (overSpec k R)).left.appLE V ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ClosedPoint

/-!
# Weil divisors on a curve and their degree

For the curve bundle `X` over a field `K`, a Weil divisor is a finitely supported
`ℤ`-valued function on the closed points (identified with the non-generic points):

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CurveDivisor`: the group of Weil divisors, `{x // x ≠ η} →₀ ℤ`,
  with its `Finsupp`-inherited `AddCommGroup` and pointwise partial order (independent of the
  base field).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg`: the degree `∑ nₓ · [κ(x) : K]`, weighted by the
  residue degrees over the base field (the correct notion over a non-closed base field), with
  additivity `deg_add` and the single-point value `deg_single`.

The residue-degree weighting is essential over a non-closed field: for `X = ℙ¹_ℝ` and the
rational function `t² + 1`, the principal divisor is `x_{t²+1} − 2·∞`, whose *unweighted*
point count is `1 − 2 = −1 ≠ 0`, while the residue-weighted degree `1·[ℂ:ℝ] − 2·[ℝ:ℝ] = 0`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

/-- A **Weil divisor** on the curve `X`: a finitely supported `ℤ`-valued function on the
closed points, identified with the non-generic points of the irreducible scheme.  Carries the
`Finsupp` `AddCommGroup` structure and the pointwise partial order.  Independent of the base
field. -/
def CurveDivisor (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] : Type u :=
  {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ

namespace CurveDivisor

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]

noncomputable instance : AddCommGroup X.CurveDivisor :=
  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup ({x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ))

instance : PartialOrder X.CurveDivisor :=
  inferInstanceAs (PartialOrder ({x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ))

section Degree

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

attribute [local instance] Scheme.residueFieldOverModule

/-- The **degree** of a Weil divisor, weighted by the residue degrees over the base field:
`deg D = ∑ₓ Dₓ · [κ(x) : K]`. -/
noncomputable def deg (D : X.CurveDivisor) : ℤ :=
  D.sum fun x n => n * (X.residueDeg K x.1 : ℤ)

@[simp]
theorem deg_zero : deg K (0 : X.CurveDivisor) = 0 := by
  simp only [deg]
  exact Finsupp.sum_zero_index

/-- Degree is additive. -/
theorem deg_add (D D' : X.CurveDivisor) : deg K (D + D') = deg K D + deg K D' := by
  simp only [deg]
  refine Finsupp.sum_add_index' (fun _ => ?_) (fun _ b₁ b₂ => ?_)
  · simp
  · ring

/-- The degree of a single-point divisor `n · x` is `n · [κ(x) : K]`. -/
theorem deg_single (x : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) (n : ℤ) :
    deg K (Finsupp.single x n : X.CurveDivisor) = n * (X.residueDeg K x.1 : ℤ) := by
  simp only [deg]
  refine Finsupp.sum_single_index ?_
  simp

/-- Degree of a negated divisor. -/
theorem deg_neg (D : X.CurveDivisor) : deg K (-D) = -deg K D := by
  have h := deg_add K D (-D)
  rw [add_neg_cancel, deg_zero] at h
  linarith

end Degree

end CurveDivisor

end Scheme

end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# A plus class becomes honest over its own étale carrier — over an ARBITRARY affine base
10	
11	This closes the obligation the CHART-U(b) header table names "honesty over a general affine
12	base" (issue I-0558), and it needs no field.
13	
14	## The obligation, and why it looked hard
15	
16	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean`'s route needs a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over an affine base
17	whose class is the (collapsed) twisted class.  `exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass`
18	(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`) supplies the datum — but it takes an **honest Čech
19	class** `c` over the base as a *hypothesis*, and a plus class over `Spec A` is not honest: it is
20	`PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E` of `A`.
21	
22	The tree's only route from a plus class to an honest one was
23	`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s `exists_splitting_of_picEt`, which requires `[Field K]` — its
24	engine is étale field-cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`),
25	false over a general base.  So the obligation read as: find a *substitute* for cofinality over
26	`Spec A`.
27	
28	## Why it is in fact free
29	
30	There is no substitute needed, because **a cover splits over its own carrier**.  The
31	field-cofinality theorem is used to produce an `A`-algebra map `E.Carrier →ₐ L` into something
32	where the class becomes a unit; but the identity `E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier` is already such a
33	map, and it exists for every cover over every base.  Restricting the plus class along
34	`A → E.Carrier` therefore makes it honest, with no finiteness, separability, or field
35	hypothesis anywhere.
36	
37	Concretely `PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x` — the
38	transported class is presented by `x` itself.  The proof is the general-base analogue of
39	`PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`), which is stated
40	only for fields; the field hypotheses there are inherited from *its* consumer (the degree seam,
41	which reads a degree and so needs a field), not required by the argument.  The one substantive
42	step is the same in both: the descent condition `x.2`, fed to `relPicAlgMap_congr`, identifies
43	the two ways of transporting `x` to the base-changed carrier.
44	
45	## What this does and does not give
46	
47	It gives honesty **over `Spec E.Carrier`**, not over `Spec A`.  That is exactly what the
48	(b-amendment) asks for — its step is "over the étale carrier `B := E.Carrier` the class is
49	honest", after which the engine fires on `Spec B` and transport (ii) pushes the open locus down
50	to `Spec A` along the (open, surjective) carrier map.  Nothing here performs that descent; the
51	topological core of it is landed as `isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage`
52	(`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean:129`).
53	
54	So after this file the CHART-U(b) route has ONE remaining obligation, the pointwise
55	`IsChartDatumPresentation` — and, unlike the previous "one remaining obligation" claims on this
56	lane, that one is a genuine statement about matching two fibre predicates, not a missing
57	construction.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self` — **a plus class is honest over its own
62	  cover carrier**, over an arbitrary affine base.
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_honest_of_picEtAff` — the existential form.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist` — the payoff, in the engine's shape: over
65	  a base where the class is honest, a datum presenting it twisted by any chart index exists.
66	-/

base-changed curve is invariant under base-field transition — for every `k`-algebra map
`φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions and every class `L` on `C_{K₁}`,

`classDeg K₂ (CechPic.map π L) = classDeg K₁ L`,

where `π := (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  Proved by the §2 ladder: reduce along the
surjective additive class map `CurveDivisor.picClass K₁` to one-point divisors, present the
point class by the tracked point equations, pull the presentation back along `π`, and close
with the fiber-degree identity (†). -/
theorem classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂)
    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left.CechPic) :
    classDeg K₂ (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) = classDeg K₁ L := by
  obtain ⟨D, rfl⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K₁ L
  suffices h : ∀ f : {p : (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left //
      p ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left} →₀ ℤ,
      classDeg K₂ (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left)
        (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₁ f))
        = classDeg K₁ (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₁ f) from h D
  intro f
  induction f using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero =>
    change classDeg K₂ (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left)
      (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₁ (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left.CurveDivisor)))
      = classDeg K₁ (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₁
        (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left.CurveDivisor))
    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, map_one, classDeg_one, classDeg_one]
  | single_add p b f hpf hb ih =>
    have key : ∀ D : (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left.CurveDivisor,
        classDeg K₂ (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left)
          (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₁ D))

/-!
# E-iv-alg: the degree is invariant under base-field transition (gap G-D5(b), SB-5)

For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` and a `k`-algebra map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field
extensions of `k`, this file proves **E-iv-alg** (`informal/deg-d5b-worksheet.md` §2):

`classDeg K₂ (CechPic.map π L) = classDeg K₁ L`

for every Čech Picard class `L` of `C_{K₁}`, along the base-field transition
`π := (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  This is the invariance equality through which the
degree of a relative Picard class becomes independent of the field of definition — the
well-definedness core of `degAt` (worksheet §1).

## The ladder (worksheet §2, steps 1–5)

1. Both sides are additive in `L`; `CurveDivisor.picClass K₁` is a surjective additive class
   map, so it suffices to treat `L = picClass K₁ (single hx' 1)` (`Finsupp.induction` plus
   `picClass_single_zpow` and `classDeg_zpow`).
2. `picClass_single` presents `L` by the tracked point equations
   `pointEquations K₁ hx' (pointUniformizerData K₁ hx')`.
3. `picClass_pullback` computes `CechPic.map π L` as the class of the pulled-back system
   `pointTransitionEquations`.  Its regularity hypothesis is discharged by
   `LocalEquations.pullbackEqn_germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: on **integral** schemes with `π`
   generic-to-generic, pulled equations are automatically regular — their germs at `η` are
   the injective function-field images of nonzero rational functions, and germs of nonzero
   sections on an integral scheme are nonzero.  (This subsumes the worksheet's
   flat-local-homomorphism discharge: integrality of both curves makes flatness of `π`
   unnecessary for regularity.)
4. The presentation divisor of the pulled system is supported in the fiber `π⁻¹(x')`, with
   coefficients `ord(π^♯ t)` (`pointTransitionEquations_presentation_elem_of_eq`/`_of_ne`:
   unit germs pull back to unit germs, the second chart piece's equation is `1`).
5. E-i (`classDeg_picClass`) turns both sides into divisor degrees, and the fiber-degree
   identity (†) (`sum_ordZ_residueDeg_baseFieldTransition`, SB-4) closes the computation.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn_germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — pulled
  local equations on integral schemes are regular (the `hreg` discharge).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointTransitionEquations`, `AlgebraicGeometry.pointTransitionUnit` —
  the pulled tracked point system and its trivializing unit `π^♯(uniformizer)`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition` — **E-iv-alg** (the keystone).

The descent gadgets (`relPicDeg` and its invariance) are in
`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.RelPicDegree`.
-/

/-!
# DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound

For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one, locally of finite type
and quasi-compact over a field `K`) carrying a **finite dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`,
there is a single integer threshold `b`, depending only on `(Y, π)` and quantified over **all**
Weil divisors `D`, past which the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes:

`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`:
`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.

This is the **P5-uniform** pre-brick of the Wave-4 datum campaign (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md`
§2.1, §4 DAT-0a). It is consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist, where the twist exponent
`M` is chosen so that `deg (Θ^M) ≥ b` and the whole degree-`g` family lands in the vanishing
locus.

## The route (worksheet §4 DAT-0a, collapsed form)

The proof is the FLV-class argument (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) with the twist specialized to the
fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and the base twist fixed at the FLV-fiber threshold `n₁` of
`D₀ = 0`:

* FLV-fiber at `D₀ = 0` (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) gives `n₁` with
  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n·F))` for all `n ≥ n₁`; take `n = n₁`, so the base twist `n₁·F` is fixed;
* `0 < deg F` (`zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`) makes `b := n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)` a legal
  threshold: for `deg D ≥ b` the residual class `[D]·[F]^{-n₁}` has degree `≥ 1 − χ`, so
  `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields an **effective** witness `E` of that class;
* `n₁·F + E` is in the class of `D`; `peel_effective` transports `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F))` to
  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F + E))`, and witness-independence
  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, W6-lite) upgrades it to `𝒪(D)`.

Because `n₁` (hence the base twist) is fixed, the effective witness carries the whole degree slack,
and `b` depends only on `(Y, π)` — exactly the shape DAT-D consumes.
-/
